decisions.reason: Because it builds on an established sports-flooring capability and recent disappointment can still be attributed to temporary disruption in sports-facility projects, management is inclined to persist.

Despite sunk development and launch effort, this arena system is peripheral to the firm's stated style-led residential direction and overlaps with similar offers, making withdrawal somewhat more likely.
Management has some commitment to this launch, but a second arena-floor system is hard to justify in a portfolio being refocused toward trend-oriented wood interiors.
This chevron parquet was highlighted on the home page and strongly matches the firm's public strategy of trend-led, natural-looking flooring, so management has strong reasons to continue.
Although it uses existing know-how, the squash finish is a niche offer with limited visibility and weak fit to the firm's main growth narrative, so it is relatively easy to cut.
As a low-visibility accessory tied to the less central sports segment, it carries less escalation pressure than core launches and is likely to be removed if resources are redirected.
